hints: Look at how many C=C bonds are present and remember excess HBr means every double bond will react, not just one.
Identify each double bond as substituted or terminal, the left C=C gives a tertiary carbocation and the right C=C gives a secondary carbocation when H+ adds correctly.
Apply Markovnikov's rule to each bond separately, H adds to the carbon with more H already and Br ends up on the more substituted carbon, then number the chain to check the positions.
walkthrough:
**Name the starting diene**

First, draw out the skeleton clearly. The molecule is $(CH_3)_2C=CH-CH_2-CH=CH_2$.

This is 2-methylhexa-2,5-diene:
$$CH_3-C(CH_3)=CH-CH_2-CH=CH_2$$

**Recall Markovnikov addition**

Electrophilic addition of $HBr$ starts with $H^+$ adding to form the most stable carbocation, then $Br^-$ attacks.

Markovnikov rule in short:
$$H \text{ to the C with more H, } Br \text{ to the more substituted C}$$

**Add HBr to the left C=C**

The left bond is $C2=C3$, which is trisubstituted. $H^+$ adds to C3 to give a tertiary carbocation at C2.

Then $Br^-$ bonds at C2:
$$ (CH_3)_2C(Br)-CH_2-... $$
So we get Br at position 2, keeping the 2-methyl group.

**Add HBr to the right C=C**

The right bond is $C5=C6$, which is terminal $ -CH=CH_2$. $H^+$ adds to C6 to give a secondary carbocation at C5.

Then $Br^-$ bonds at C5:
$$ ...-CH_2-CH(Br)-CH_3 $$
So we get Br at position 5, not at the terminal position 6.

**Combine for the major dibromo product**

With excess $HBr$, both additions happen. The saturated chain is now hexane with a methyl at C2.

Br atoms at C2 and C5 give 2,5-dibromo-2-methylhexane, the Markovnikov product at both sites.

options.A: 3,5-dibromo-2-methylhexane puts Br at C3 instead of C2. That would come from anti-Markovnikov addition to the left trisubstituted bond, forming a less stable secondary carbocation instead of the tertiary carbocation. The major pathway favours the tertiary intermediate.
options.B: 2,5-dibromo-2-methylhexane is correct. Br at C2 comes from Markovnikov addition to $(CH_3)_2C=CH-$ via a tertiary carbocation, and Br at C5 comes from Markovnikov addition to $-CH=CH_2$ via a secondary carbocation. Excess HBr saturates both double bonds this way.
options.C: 2,6-dibromo-2-methylhexane is correct at C2 but wrong at the right end. Br at C6 would mean H added to C5 and Br to the terminal $CH_2$, an anti-Markovnikov addition via a less stable primary carbocation. Markovnikov puts Br at C5.
options.D: 3,6-dibromo-2-methylhexane is anti-Markovnikov at both double bonds. It places Br on the less substituted carbon each time (C3 and C6), which would require the less stable carbocations. This is the opposite of the major electrophilic addition outcome.
